model: PowerXL DA1 variable frequency drive (Modbus RTU)
applies_to: Eaton PowerXL DA1 per the Modbus RTU communication manual MN040018EN, edition 12/22.
summary: The PowerXL DA1 talks Modbus RTU on its RJ45 RS-485 socket. Eaton numbers every value by an ID: a small process-data block (command, speed reference, status/fault word, speed, current) plus parameter IDs. Every value is a single 16-bit register with an implied decimal point. This map covers the process data and the communication settings.

addressing.note: The manual numbers registers from ID 1. Its frame examples read status ID 6 with start address 0005h and write command ID 1 to address 0000h, so ID n is wire address n-1.

source.title: PowerXL Modbus RTU Communication manual for Variable Frequency Drives / Variable Speed Starters DA1, DB1, DC1, DE1
source.pages: Enable and data format p. 9; DA1 comms parameters pp. 11-12; register mapping p. 27; process data pp. 28-39; frame examples pp. 40-41; DA1 parameter table pp. 42-52

notes: Every value is one 16-bit register; the decimal point is implied (a displayed 0.3 A is sent as 3).
The manual does not state signedness for the process data; they are typed UINT16 because their ranges are non-negative (direction is a status bit).

Output power (ID 10) is left out: the summary table gives scale 1 but the detailed text says one decimal (53 = 5.3 kW). The power (ID 13) and voltage range (ID 14) words are left out because their meaning depends on the drive's kW/HP setting.

Fault numbers in the high byte of ID 6 for the DA1 (decimal, as printed in table 11): 0 no-Flt (no fault), 1 OI-b brake overcurrent, 2 OL-br brake resistor overload, 3 O-I output overcurrent, 4 I.t-trP motor overload, 5 PS-trp hardware overcurrent, 6 O.Volt DC overvoltage, 7 U.Volt DC undervoltage, 8 O-t heatsink overtemperature, 9 U-t undertemperature, 10 P-dEf defaults loaded, 11 E-trip external fault, 12 SC-ObS keypad/PC comms error, 13 FlT-dc DC ripple too high, 14 P-LOss input phase loss, 15 h O-I output overcurrent, 16 Th-flt heatsink thermistor fault, 17 dAtA-F memory error, 18 4-20 F analog input out of range, 19 dAtA-E memory error, 20 U-dEf user defaults loaded, 21 F-Ptc motor PTC, 22 FAn-F fan fault, 23 O-hEAt ambient too hot, 24 O-torQ torque too high, 25 U-torQ torque too low (hoist brake), 26 OUt-F output fault, 29 Sto-F STO circuit fault, 30-35 Enc-01..06 encoder faults, 40-44 AtF-01..05 motor identification failed, 49 Out-Ph motor phase lost, 50 Sc-FO1 Modbus timeout, 51 Sc-FO2 CANopen timeout, 52 Sc-FO3 fieldbus option lost, 53 Sc-F04 I/O option lost, 60-61 OF-01/OF-02 option card faults, 70-74 PLC-01..05 function-block editor faults. The 'Stop' display (enable signal missing) is listed without a number and is not a fault.

Left out: t-acc/t-dec (P1-03/P1-04), whose scale is printed as 300 = 30.0 s while the range column reads 0.00-6000 s; the fixed-frequency and f-max/f-min registers (60 counts per Hz); heatsink temperature (no data format, so signedness is unknown) and the MWh meter (no scale or data format); serial number words 25-28.
The DA1 also has user registers 51-78 for its function-block editor; they are not mapped.

registers.name: Fieldbus command
registers.description: Control word: run, direction, reset, coast, quick stop.

registers.name: Fieldbus speed reference
registers.description: Setpoint frequency, limited to the min/max frequency parameters.

registers.name: Status and fault word
registers.description: Low byte = status bits, high byte = fault number.

bits.8-15: Fault word: the fault number (see notes), 0 = no fault

registers.name: Digital inputs
registers.description: Input states; the lowest bit is DI1.

registers.name: Drive type code
registers.description: Part-number code: frame size, voltage class, phases and power index as hex digits.

registers.name: Local process data source
registers.description: Selects where run commands and the speed reference come from.

values.4: Fieldbus control (Modbus RTU if no fieldbus option)
values.5: Server mode (follows a drive in client mode)
values.13: SmartWire-DT control and reference, digital input enables

registers.name: Modbus comms timeout
registers.description: Time without a valid telegram before P5-06 acts.

values.1: Ramp to stop, then switch off

integration.summary: Write the speed reference to ID 2 and the command word to ID 1 (bit 0 = run), then read IDs 6-8 for status, speed and current. The control-source parameter must select Modbus first.
integration.enable: Set P1-12 = 4 (fieldbus control; Modbus RTU when no fieldbus option is fitted). The STO input acts as the enable signal. Address P5-01, baud P5-03, parity P5-04.
integration.watchdog: P5-05 sets the comms timeout in 0.1 s steps and P5-06 the reaction: trip, ramp then trip, ramp without fault, or run at P2-08.
quirks: Register = ID - 1 on the wire; tools with a +1 offset take the ID directly.
Function codes 03, 06, 16 and 23 only; at most 11 registers per read.
The high byte of ID 6 is a fault number, not flags.
setup: P5-01 = address (default 1), P5-03 = baud (default 4 = 115.2 kbit/s), P5-04 = parity (default no parity, 1 stop bit).
The RS-485 link is on the RJ45 socket.
gotchas: Without the DI1/STO enable the drive reports 'Stop' and will not run from Modbus.
Set bit 2 of the command word to reset a fault.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
